mechanism_narrative: The sustained and accelerating decline in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a deepening trend of reduced consumer activity. This momentum will persist, driving further decreases in retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed negative trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in PARKS mobility below -20% suggests a strong shift away from outdoor leisure activities, likely due to colder weather or increased caution. This reduction in general outdoor movement will translate to lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as people stay home.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20% in the last week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than over the last 14 days, despite the sharp decline in PARKS mobility.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases, while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high and WORKPLACES mobility remains low.

mechanism_narrative: The continuous decline in TRANSIT station visits reflects reduced public transport usage, often a precursor or consequence of tightening public health measures or increased public apprehension. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises, despite TRANSIT mobility continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility falls below 2%, it signals that even essential trips are being minimized, indicating a high level of caution or restriction. candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 2% in the last week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next 7 days increases, even though GROCERY_PHARM mobility was below 2% in the last week.
